panels.title: Block tip age
panels.description: now() - latest_block_timestamp

panels.title: Blocks indexed per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of block_full_processing_duration_microseconds_count — one observation per block processed

panels.title: Transactions per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of transactions_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 on each successful block import

panels.title: Internal transactions per second
panels.description: rate of internal_transactions_imported_count — incremented on each successful import in Indexer.Fetcher.InternalTransaction

panels.title: Logs per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of logs_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 on each successful block import

panels.title: Blocks imported per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of blocks_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 by the block batch size on each successful import. Block-level analogue of transactions_imported_count.

panels.title: Blocks internal-tx-indexed per second
panels.description: rate of blocks_internal_transactions_indexed_count — incremented in Indexer.Fetcher.InternalTransaction by the unique block count of each successful batch. Block-level analogue of internal_transactions_imported_count.

panels.title: Block full processing latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: avg = rate(sum)/rate(count), the exact arithmetic mean (bucket-independent, throughput-relevant). max-bucket = histogram_quantile(1.0,...), the upper edge of the highest non-empty bucket — answers "are observations landing in the slow bucket?". Histograms don't store true sample min/max, so quantile-based panels were dropped; the legend's "max" column shows the per-series maximum of the avg over the time range.

panels.title: Block import (DB write) latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: Wall-clock duration of Chain.import — INCLUDES DB-pool checkout, BEGIN, all upserts (and any row-lock waits from concurrent writers), and COMMIT. No advisory locks in this path, so the metric already captures lock-wait time. Avg is the throughput-relevant figure; max-bucket flags when batches land in the slow bucket.

panels.title: Batch fetch (JSON-RPC) latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: JSON-RPC batch fetch round-trip from the block fetcher.

panels.title: Legacy single-phase fetch latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: internal_transactions_fetch_duration_microseconds — single-phase JSON-RPC round-trip for trace_block / debug_trace per BufferedTask batch. Only populated for non-Geth variants (Nethermind/Erigon/Besu/RSK/Filecoin) or :transaction_params mode. EMPTY when Geth two-phase debug_traceBlockByNumber is active — see the Phase 1 raw HTTP / Phase 2 decode panels below instead.

panels.title: Internal-tx import (Chain.import) latency (avg / last-sample max)
panels.description: internal_transactions_import_duration_* — Chain.import call duration for an internal-tx batch (success or failure). Avg is computed from rate(_sum)/rate(_count). "last" is a gauge of the most recent observation; max_over_time samples it across scrapes, so single outliers between scrapes may be missed (use the gate_hold panel for tail-resistant visibility). Climbing avg = Postgres or sub-multi fan-out is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Missing data (blocks / internal txs / token balances)
Indexed tip vs node tip
panels.description: latest_block_number is the indexer's tip; node tip = indexer + delay_from_last_node_block-equivalent block. Plot both side by side.

panels.title: Internal-tx indexing errors by block range (100k bucket)
panels.description: Heatmap of rate(internal_transactions_indexing_errors_count) summed across stages, by 100k-block bucket. Row label is reconstructed to the bucket's starting block number by appending 5 zeros to the block_range_100k bucket value (e.g. bucket 132 → label 13200000 = blocks 13,200,000–13,299,999). Bright cells = blocks in that range currently failing internal-tx indexing (RPC or DB). Pair with the stage breakdown to identify root cause, and with `SELECT min/max(block_number) FROM pending_block_operations` to confirm the stuck range.

panels.title: Internal-tx indexing errors by stage
panels.description: rate(internal_transactions_indexing_errors_count) broken down by stage (rpc_fetch vs db_import). Tells you whether the node or the database is the bottleneck — the heatmap to the left shows where in the chain.

panels.title: Phase 1 — raw HTTP fetch latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: internal_transactions_raw_fetch_duration_microseconds — HTTP round-trip only, NO gunzip / NO Jason.decode. Should be much smaller than the legacy `Internal-tx fetch (JSON-RPC) latency` panel. If avg climbs here the RPC node is the bottleneck; if it stays flat while throughput drops, look at phase 2.

panels.title: Phase 2 — decode + transform latency (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: internal_transactions_decode_duration_microseconds — gunzip + Jason.decode + trace flattening + transform, run under HeavyStageGate. Bounded by permit count; if this saturates and `Heavy-stage gate wait` climbs, raise INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS — at the cost of higher peak memory.

panels.title: Heavy-stage gate wait (avg / max-bucket)
panels.description: internal_transactions_heavy_gate_wait_duration_microseconds — time a BufferedTask task spends parked at HeavyStageGate before acquiring a permit. Sustained nonzero values = gate is the bottleneck. Knobs: raise INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS (more memory) or lower INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_CONCURRENCY / BATCH_SIZE (less pipeline pressure).

panels.title: Heavy-stage gate permits in use
panels.description: internal_transactions_heavy_gate_in_use gauge — number of decode/import slots currently held. Plateaus at INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS when saturated. If this is consistently below the permit count, the gate isn't the bottleneck — look at RPC fetch or DB import latency instead.

panels.title: Gate hold vs decode latency — what the permit really protects
panels.description: The HeavyStageGate's permit is held from acquisition through decode + Chain.import + bookkeeping. "gate_hold" measures the full hold duration; "decode" measures only the gunzip+Jason.decode+transform step. The gap between them is the time the gate is serializing work other than decode — typically Chain.import and its parallel sub-multis. A persistent large gap means the gate is doing more than its memory-containment job. Avg uses rate(_sum)/rate(_count). "last-max" is max_over_time of the latest-value gauge — Prometheus samples at scrape time so very brief outliers can be missed.

panels.title: Raw response body size — compressed (avg / max-bucket, bytes)
panels.description: internal_transactions_raw_body_bytes — size of each debug_traceBlockByNumber HTTP body (compressed if ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_HTTP_GZIP_ENABLED=true, else uncompressed). Bounds the memory held by parked tasks waiting on HeavyStageGate. Spiking max-bucket = batches landing in the largest size bucket — consider lowering INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_BATCH_SIZE.

panels.title: Decompressed body size (avg / max-bucket, bytes)
panels.description: internal_transactions_decompressed_body_bytes — size of each debug_traceBlockByNumber response after gunzip, one observation per HTTP round-trip. Peak Elixir-term memory during decode ≈ max-bucket × HeavyStageGate permits. Divide by the compressed panel's avg for the wire-compression ratio (typically 10–50× for trace payloads).

panels.title: Buffer queue size
panels.description: Total items the InternalTransaction BufferedTask currently holds in memory across current_buffer, current_front_buffer and bound_queue. Near zero for an extended period while indexing is supposed to be active = BufferedTask is starved (typically poll:false + no block imports calling async_fetch). A restart re-runs init and refills.

panels.title: Buffer block — min
panels.description: Lowest block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state.

panels.title: Buffer block — max
panels.description: Highest block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state.

panels.title: Last indexed block
panels.description: Highest block_number from the most recently imported internal-tx batch. Flat line while pipeline stages are non-zero = imports stalled. With FETCH_ORDER=desc this hugs the chain tip as a freshly populated batch always carries the highest available block.

panels.title: Buffer queue size over time
panels.description: Total items the BufferedTask is holding in memory. Drops to zero while indexing is supposed to be active = starvation: init's one-shot stream completed and nothing is refilling the buffer.

panels.title: Buffer block range + last indexed
panels.description: Min and max block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state, plus the last successfully imported block. With FETCH_ORDER=desc the buffer max stays near chain tip and the min drifts down as catchup progresses.

panels.title: Stage time spent per second (worker-equivalents)
panels.description: sum(rate(<metric>_sum)) / 1e6 for each duration histogram — total wall-clock work performed in each stage per wall-clock second, measured in worker-equivalents. A value of N means the stage is doing N seconds of work per second, i.e. it requires N workers running fully busy. Compare against each stage's configured concurrency (block fetcher pool size, INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_CONCURRENCY, INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS, DB pool size) — the stage whose load is closest to its limit is the throughput bottleneck. This is the most reliable saturation signal in the dashboard.
